chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Only a mistaken person monopolizes food."
ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about food monopoly (hukrah) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In the context of *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) via his father Imam al-Baqir (AS) defines *hukrah* (monopoly/hoarding) as a distinct economic sin, characterizing the hoarder as *khati'*—one who errs in both religious duty and market ethics. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on preventing artificial scarcity to protect the community's welfare, linking economic behavior directly to spiritual integrity and divine provision.
